item.description:
Note:
  • The dashboard rebuilds once on the first launch after updating. The saved snapshot now records which scan roots produced it, so a snapshot written by the previous version is not restored. Expect one cold start and nothing else.
  • Downgrading after this release sets your quota pace history aside. The store that records those readings moves to a new format, and an older TokenBar cannot read it — it moves the file to a quarantine copy beside it and starts over, so the pace cards go back to learning. Nothing is deleted: that copy holds the complete history and the data is recoverable. Usage totals are unaffected either way, because those are read from your logs. The conversion happens on the next write the app had a reason to make, so a file still reading schemaVersion 3 for a while after updating is normal and not a failed migration.
Features:
  • Quota gets its own lens. A window card draws the subscription's quota over time with the local usage that moved it underneath, so a flat stretch of quota can be read against the work that was or was not happening. Alongside it: Window history lists recent reset cycles for the open subscription, each expandable to a per-model breakdown; Past windows on the all-agent view shows a strip of cycle bars per quota window; an estimate says what 10% of the allowance is worth in tokens and dollars; a weekday heatmap shows when the allowance is spent; and a summary card carries the shape of it to Overview. Quota window rows also carry a recent-trend indicator, and Overview cards can be hidden individually apart from the usage chart, which stays as the lens's anchor.
  • A model-scoped quota window now counts only its model. Claude reports scoped weekly limits such as "Fable only", and the usage drawn under those windows was the whole subscription's. The bars, the history rows and the cost estimate now all narrow to the model the allowance charges. When nothing local matches that model the card says so, rather than drawing an empty week.
  • Claude scan roots can be added in Settings. A second Claude account kept under its own CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR is invisible to a scan that only reads the default location. Those directories can now be registered, and unreachable ones are kept and retried rather than dropped.
  • A second Claude account gets its own quota card and its own history. An account kept under its own CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR is fetched, identified and recorded separately, so each card carries its own plan label and its own recorded cycles. One limit is deliberate: when an additional account's token expires TokenBar does not refresh it in place, and the card says so and asks you to run claude under that CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR. Refreshing it in place would write that account's token over your main account's stored credential and log you out of the main account, so it fails closed instead.
  • A weekly quota window now records a reading about every hour instead of about every 3.5 hours, and a window sitting at its full allowance records that starting point instead of waiting for the first spend.
Fixes:
  • Opening and closing the popover repeatedly no longer risks Anthropic's rate limit. Three independent callers fetched the quota payload, each written to call first and sleep after, and the popover's loop restarted on every open — so ten opens issued ten requests with nothing in between. Requests now share a floor and concurrent callers share one request. A slow request is timed from when it returned, not from when it was asked, so the protection does not dissolve exactly while the endpoint is struggling.
  • Usage from a previous account no longer survives a change of credential target. Switching the durable authentication target left the prior account's usage on screen until something else replaced it.
  • The cycle still running no longer appears under past windows. It was listed beside completed cycles and counted toward the estimate while still filling, so an estimate could move while being read.
  • A source you excluded is no longer reported back as unclassified. Excluding a source is a classification, and the line that names what else was in a window said the opposite.
  • Launching no longer throws away work it had already done. Registering your Claude directories with the engine happens at every launch and on every settings save, not only when something changed, and it dropped every cached scan result, forced a reload, and re-fetched every quota — regardless. So an ordinary launch paid to rebuild what it already had, and spent provider requests doing it. All of that now happens only when the registered directories actually differ, with one deliberate exception: the first registration after a launch still refreshes the quota cards, because the engine starts each run with none registered and the menu bar can otherwise show a reading taken before your extra account was known.
  • Two Claude accounts no longer interfere with each other's rate-limit backoff or profile cache. A shared cooldown meant one account clearing it lifted it for the other, and a shared profile entry collapsed its one-hour lifetime into a fetch on every poll. Single-account users are unaffected.
  • A count of zero is no longer shown where nothing was counted. A source that reports a price with no token counts rendered as a measured zero beside a real dollar amount, in the quota history rows, their expanded per-model rows, and the subscription trend under its token metric.

Note:
  • Amp, Cursor, OpenClaw, MiMoCode, and Mux rescan once after this update. Their cached data is rebuilt from scratch on the first refresh because the engine update advances their parser identity. Expect one slower scan for those clients; other clients keep their cache.
Fixes:
  • A Claude credential store that holds no login no longer blocks the setup-token fallback. A "Claude Code-credentials" Keychain item that exists but carries no claudeAiOauth key, such as one holding only MCP server OAuth data, was read as a damaged credential and failed closed, so the documented tokenbar-claude-oauth-token path was never tried and the card stayed on "Claude credentials could not be loaded." Such a store is now treated as absence, while a credential whose claudeAiOauth is present but unusable still fails closed.
  • Manual refresh now retries a model report that failed. The Refresh button and Command-R refreshed the graph and any loaded Hourly or Agents report but stopped short of the model report, so a transient failure stayed on screen until the next 60-second poll even right after the user asked for fresh data. A refresh that wanted a model report now retries it in the same pass, provided the graph itself refreshed successfully.
  • Reopening the popover no longer shows the previous window's data. Closing it during a scan let the retiring view finish and write its result into the shared reopen cache after a newer view had already committed, so the next open rendered the older payload.
  • Entries with no usage are no longer offered for classification. Usage attribution listed a row for every observed source key, so a row reading 0 tokens and $0.00 asked which subscription had paid for nothing. An entry with no tokens and no cost is now dropped, per entry and before entries are folded into a source, and a range left with nothing says so instead. An entry with zero tokens but non-zero cost is kept, and a source whose entries cancel out still appears, because each of those entries is real.
Changes:
  • Three client names no longer claim a surface their data does not distinguish: Codex CLI becomes Codex, Copilot CLI becomes Copilot, and Cursor IDE becomes Cursor. Each card reads a source that covers several surfaces at once. Across 1,733 local Codex session files the actual CLI was roughly 4% of what the card labelled "Codex CLI".
  • Usage attribution now says that some clients merge related routes before the page sees them, with Vertex AI arriving as Anthropic and Codex as OpenAI. A row that arrived already merged cannot be split there, and whether a row is affected depends on the client that produced it. The page previously told only the exact-comparison half.
  • Engine update: the shared usage engine advances to a reviewed revision carrying local-first graph pricing, embedded and partial cost provenance, message-only cost coverage, and preservation of Kilo's provider-reported cost. The cache format, the FFI boundary, and result decoding are unchanged. One part is visible in your numbers: a Trae row whose payload carries no usable dollar amount was previously left unpriced and is now estimated under the default best-effort pricing, so a Trae total can rise without your usage having changed. Provider-reported values remain authoritative.

Note:
  • Pace history restarts once with this update. A card returns to "Learning history" and rebuilds unless its provider gives TokenBar a stable account identifier, which today means Codex with an account ID on its credential, and the Antigravity IDE. This is the cost of the identity fix below and it happens only once.
Fixes:
  • Pace history no longer restarts every time another app refreshes a shared login. Providers without a stable account identifier kept losing their learned usage curve whenever the Claude CLI or a sibling tool rotated the credential they share, so Historical pace could never accumulate.
  • A pace marker in deficit is now highlighted whether it came from the historical curve or the linear estimate. Previously only a historical result was coloured, so the warning appeared and disappeared as the fit requalified while the deficit itself never moved.
  • A clock disagreement no longer discards the whole quota history. A single forward jump of the system clock, from a time sync or a sleep and wake, could leave one window with a timestamp ahead of the next read, which quarantined every provider's history at once. It is now repaired in place, and only genuinely unverifiable data is dropped.
Improved:
  • Updater: the bundled Sparkle framework is now compiled from source as part of the build.

Fixes:
  • The Discord agent picker no longer lists every agent TokenBar recognises. It used to offer a row for each one, including agents you had never run and agents you had hidden, and naming one of those left the presence empty without saying why.

New:
  • TokenBar can publish what you are working on to Discord. It is off by default. You choose which of today's tokens, the agent and the cost band it shows, and which agent by name; all three are shown unless you change them.
  • A Usage attribution page in Settings lets you declare which subscription a client's local usage belongs to. Running another provider's model through an agent is common, and the usage was previously drawn against that agent's own quota. Stats now breaks the total into assigned, excluded and undeclared.
Improved:
  • Opening the popover no longer waits for two extra scans. The chart runs on its own and appears as soon as it is ready.
  • Scanning is faster: on an 8 GB history, a cold scan dropped about 31 percent and a warm scan about 37 percent. Peak memory is about 15 percent higher, which is the trade for the parallel parsing.
  • Restarting shows your last dashboard immediately and refreshes behind it, instead of showing nothing for several seconds.
  • Turns that an in-place transcript rewrite used to drop are now kept. This does not restore history already lost. A total can still fall on the first launch if a transcript was compacted since the last scan, because the rebuild reads the file as it stands now.
Fixes:
  • Inactive segments of the view switch are clickable again.
  • Codex shows its monochrome mark instead of the ChatGPT green.
  • Hovering a heatmap cell rings it, the way the bar chart already did.

Note: the first launch after this update rescans every client once, because the engine's cache format changed. Later launches are back to normal.

Thanks: @yeha98555

New:
  • Brand logos for the Cline, jcode, MiMo Code, and gjc tabs, instead of a letter badge.
Improved:
  • The client-tab row now scrolls with a plain vertical mouse wheel, so a mouse without a horizontal-scroll wheel can reach every tab.
Fixes:
  • Antigravity CLI now shows the shared Antigravity quota instead of an empty or duplicate limit card.

New:
  • Tracks five more local AI coding tools: Cline, Antigravity CLI, jcode, MiMo Code, and gjc.
Improved:
  • More accurate cost and per-tool attribution across AI token usage.
  • Corrected Codex usage counts for forked and sub-agent sessions.
  • Antigravity CLI usage is now dated per turn, so the live view and daily totals reflect when each turn actually happened.
Fixes:
  • The app no longer crashes if the usage parser hits an unexpected error.
  • More reliable live usage updates, including for the newly added tools.
